title: Daily physics — Wednesday, 11 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart; this is an inferred ranking, not a readership or download ranking, and citation evidence is sparse for papers this recent.

sections.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
sections.abstract: The ARA Collaboration reports its first array-wide diffuse ultra-high-energy neutrino search, finding no candidates and setting a stringent flux upper limit from 50 to 1000 EeV.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe zero passing events on an expected background of 0.13 (+0.01/-0.01 statistical, +0.05/-0.06 systematic) and report the strongest limit from 50–1000 EeV, excluding some trans-GZK proton-source models at 90% confidence.
sections.evidence_type: observational; 10.6 years of ARA array-wide livetime (January 2013–December 2023), all five stations, with detector and neutrino simulations
sections.unique_caveat: This is a null search, not a neutrino detection. Exposure depends on ice and Askaryan-emission models and the neutrino–nucleon cross section; the companion analysis reports substantial high-energy acceptance uncertainties.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The neutrino-focused Global-Nu daily digest highlighted this result; it combines the full five-station ARA array and decade-scale exposure with a concrete flux constraint. The companion methodology paper is part of the same analysis, not an independent confirmation.

sections.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: The authors use 63 superconducting qubits to measure real-time electric-string dynamics in a two-dimensional Z₂ gauge theory with dynamical matter across confined and deconfined regimes.
sections.claimed_result: Spatially resolved measurements show rapid charge/flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation near a pair-creation resonance, and reduced spreading at strong electric fields; the authors use Gauss-law constraints as an error-detection resource.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; a 5×4 matter-site lattice on a 63-qubit superconducting processor, with up to 15 second-order Trotter steps and ancilla checks
sections.unique_caveat: The finite lattice and short evolution limit extrapolation to larger systems and longer times; tensor-network comparisons converge only over a shorter time range, while hardware noise grows at later steps.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent public writeups appeared at Quantum.world and Quantum Zeitgeist; the paper also demonstrates a comparatively large superconducting processor on a concrete many-body gauge problem.

sections.title: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moiré rhombohedral graphene
sections.abstract: Electrical-transport and noise measurements in hole-doped moiré rhombohedral graphene reveal incommensurate Chern-insulating states and signatures consistent with an anomalous Hall crystal.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret Chern insulators at incommensurate hole densities, together with current-induced broadband noise, memory effects, gate hysteresis, and field/temperature dependence, as experimental evidence for a spontaneously charge-ordered parent state.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; electrical transport and noise measurements with systematic magnetic-field, temperature, and gate dependence
sections.unique_caveat: The charge-order interpretation is inferred from transport and noise signatures rather than direct real-space imaging; the authors call for scanning-probe studies and note that twist-angle/moiré dependence needs further study.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three condensed-matter subfields and reports a direct transport/noise experiment on a debated topological phase; these are scientific-significance signals rather than measured readership.

sections.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
sections.abstract: A new von Mises–Fisher analysis of Pierre Auger ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray arrival directions searches consistently for excesses across angular scales using the Observatory’s full Phase I dataset.
sections.claimed_result: The most significant excess is a dipolar modulation at 8–16 EeV, compatible with earlier Auger findings; above 32 EeV the authors find indications of a Centaurus-region intermediate-scale excess alongside the dipole.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Pierre Auger Observatory Phase I events above 4 EeV collected from January 2004 through December 2022
sections.unique_caveat: The Centaurus feature is not a source identification, and the authors say composition information and more data are needed to distinguish source-population and mixed-composition explanations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The analysis uses the full 2004–2022 Phase I sample (123,000 km² sr yr exposure) and supplies a method joining large- and intermediate-scale searches; its higher-energy Centaurus feature is explicitly described as an indication, not a detection.

sections.title: The unified bound dark energy–bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
sections.abstract: The authors fit a unified dark-sector model to DESI DR2 BAO, CMB and lensing measurements, and Unite supernovae, reporting parameter constraints and comparisons with ΛCDM and w₀wₐCDM.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find the full combination statistically equivalent to ΛCDM and w₀wₐCDM, while the bound-dark-matter variant is moderately favored over cold dark matter within their model; they propose future high-redshift and small-scale measurements as discriminants.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; model fitting to DESI DR2 BAO, Planck/ACT DR6/SPT-3G CMB spectra, ACT+SPT lensing, and Unite supernova data
sections.unique_caveat: The inference is model-dependent, and the reported preference for bound dark matter is internal to this model comparison; the authors find no decisive preference over standard dark-energy models in the full data combination.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It combines several current cosmological datasets and reports quantified model comparisons and a constrained dark-matter velocity parameter; these are scientific-content signals, not independent evidence of popularity.
